sections.summary: Paul argues that even the most impressive spiritual abilities — tongues of angels, prophetic powers, all knowledge, mountain-moving faith, radical self-sacrifice — amount to 'nothing' without love, establishing love as the indispensable condition for any gift to have value.

Paul describes love through fifteen predicates — what it does and does not do — creating a portrait that functions as a diagnostic mirror exposing the Corinthians' failures of envy, boasting, arrogance, rudeness, and insistence on their own way.

sections.section_title: The Permanence of Love and the Temporality of Gifts
sections.summary: Paul contrasts the permanence of love, which never ends, with the temporality of prophecy, tongues, and knowledge, which will cease when the complete comes, using the metaphor of childhood and adulthood and the contrast between seeing in a mirror dimly and seeing face to face.
Paul concludes that faith, hope, and love abide — these three — and the greatest of these is love, establishing love's supremacy over all other qualities including faith itself.
